title: 1-Framework: Finding the Parts I Should Stop Rebuilding
author: Jason Lamb
excerpt: My architectural baseline for sharing PHP and JSON conventions across small apps without forcing every project into a rewrite.

cover.alt: 1-Framework: Finding the Parts I Should Stop Rebuilding cover image

content_html:
After building several small applications, the repeated work becomes hard to ignore. Authentication, configuration, logging, audit records, and shared styling keep returning under different project names. 1-Framework is where I am organizing a more reusable approach.

The goal is a PHP and JSON foundation that fits shared hosting and does not require a database server. The project separates responsibilities into core utilities, configuration, authentication, logging, auditing, assets, and storage conventions.

The current status needs to be stated plainly: this is an architectural baseline. The documentation defines responsibilities and a path toward extracting functional modules. It is not a finished framework whose features have already been rolled into every app in the repository.

The adoption plan is deliberately incremental. Identify a reusable component, extract it without changing the original project, remove project-specific assumptions, document it, and validate it independently. Then integrate it into a small application before trying broader adoption.

One rule is particularly useful: a shared component must not depend on a specific application. A warranty tracker can depend on the foundation; the foundation should not secretly depend on the warranty tracker's field names.

This project also gives AI-assisted development clearer conventions to work within. A consistent response format or storage rule is easier to follow when it is written down instead of rediscovered in each conversation.

The aim is less repeated setup and fewer slightly different solutions to the same backend problem. It is the workshop organization project behind the other workshop projects—and, like organizing a real workshop, it has to make the next job easier to justify its own space.
